programme.title: Morning Tea in Wuzhong
programme.desc: This documentary explores Wuzhong's unique morning tea culture from an international perspective. Through compelling stories, it showcases the city’s charming landscapes, inclusive atmosphere and the everyday lives of its residents.

programme.title: Gourmets Alive II Ep.5
programme.desc: Literati such as Lu You, Li Yu, Yuan Mei, and Wang Zengqi take center stage as we explore their worlds and works through the flavors and cuisine of daily life.

programme.title: From Farm to Table (China-France Season) Ep.3
programme.desc: Set against the backdrop of the 60th anniversary of Sino-French diplomatic relations, this program focuses on the full-chain coordination mechanism that brings food from French farms to Chinese tables, capturing the collision and fusion of two great food cultures.

programme.title: Foodwise: Xilingol
programme.desc: The Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region is located in the northern part of China, stretching from northeast to southwest side. In Xilin Gol, the horses, sheep and cows could be found every where. The local cuisines here are so attractive to the tourists, such as the roasted lamb is a traditional local dish. And the fired stone fried lamb is so hard to find if you are not traveling to Inner Mongolia. Have you ever tried salted milk tea? Just join in this visual trip！

programme.title: China Bound: Suzhou
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He visits Suzhou, a historic city in eastern China famously admired by Marco Polo. Crisscrossed by canals, Suzhou is renowned for its exquisite gardens, where ancient scholars recreated nature's beauty within their own homes. Tianran discovers a city of refined tastes, where even a bowl of breakfast noodles comes with unspoken etiquette, locals insist on only in-season produce, and foodies eagerly await the arrival of prized hairy crabs.

programme.title: All About the Yak
programme.desc: In this episode, we go to Nangqian, Yushu, Qinghai Province, to get close contact with the Yak in Tibet, which is known as the "Vehicle on the Plateau". During the bustling yak culture festival, people gather from near and far, meadows are crowded, and yak appraisal activities are also in full swing. As the journey continues, we are able to understand several aspects of the yak culture which is closely related to the life of Tibetan people.

programme.title: Between Heaven and Earth : Traveling Through Grasslands Ep.3
programme.desc: The first season of the "Wandering the World" series follows a traveler across six of China's greatest grasslands, revealing the natural beauty of their epic landscapes and the distinctive lives of the people who inhabit them.

programme.title: Miao Embroidery: History in Stitches
programme.desc: According to legend, during a migration by the Miao ethnic group, a female chieftain wanted to keep a record of all the mountains and lakes she passed along the way. The means she chose of doing so was by stitching the images on her dress. By the time they reached a suitable place to settle, her clothing was covered with embroidered designs. This, it's said, was the origin of Miao embroidery. As the story tells us, the designs in Miao embroidery are closely related to the natural world and daily life. The Miao people have a special fondness for nature. So, as well as depicting their daily farming and work activities, they copy birds, flowers, mountains, and grass onto their clothing. Over the years, the embroidery of the Miao people has become a written record of their life. The stitches are like characters which, when many of them are combined, become a record of their history, their collected wisdom, and the knowledge passed down from their ancestors.

programme.title: Exploring the Folklore of Chongqing
programme.desc: Exploring the Folklore of Chongqing delves into the historical origins and cultural background of Fengdu Ghost City, and also features the Zhongyuan Festival celebrations and ancestor - worshipping rituals held here. These activities reflect the local people's positive and optimistic outlook on life and death, as well as the great importance they attach to their ancestors, families and family traditions.

programme.title: Aerial China IV: Hong Kong
programme.desc: Hong Kong, a city of skyscrapers positively pulsing with financial energy, the legendary Pearl of the Orient. But there’s another side to that great city - the nighttime romance of Victoria Harbour, islands frozen in time for hundreds of millions of years, a metropolis constantly changing and transforming itself. Join us for the ultimate bird’s eyes of Hong Kong!

programme.title: Shunde's Waterways: where business smarts meet everyday life
programme.desc: Shunde, a district in Guangdong Province, lies in the Pearl River Delta, north of Hong Kong - a water-rich region that lives by water and knows how to turn it into opportunity. Once, boats carried silk down its canals from small villages, building a legacy of trade. Today, Xiangyunsha (gambiered Canton gauze) is a global fashion icon, and historic spots like Mingshi Garden draw tourists and locals alike. With water as their muse and grit as their guide, Shunde folks keep business thriving while making life sweeter - that's the quiet wisdom flowing through their rivers. Now, two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia are setting out to explore more with the locals...

Crisscrossed by canals, Suzhou is renowned for its exquisite gardens, where ancient scholars recreated nature's beauty within their own homes. Tianran discovers a city of refined tastes, where even a bowl of breakfast noodles comes with unspoken etiquette, locals insist on only in-season produce, and foodies eagerly await the arrival of prized hairy crabs.

programme.title: All About the Yak
programme.desc: In this episode, we go to Nangqian, Yushu, Qinghai Province, to get close contact with the Yak in Tibet, which is known as the "Vehicle on the Plateau". During the bustling yak culture festival, people gather from near and far, meadows are crowded, and yak appraisal activities are also in full swing. As the journey continues, we are able to understand several aspects of the yak culture which is closely related to the life of Tibetan people.

programme.title: Between Heaven and Earth : Traveling Through Grasslands Ep.3
programme.desc: The first season of the "Wandering the World" series follows a traveler across six of China's greatest grasslands, revealing the natural beauty of their epic landscapes and the distinctive lives of the people who inhabit them.

programme.title: Miao Embroidery: History in Stitches
programme.desc: According to legend, during a migration by the Miao ethnic group, a female chieftain wanted to keep a record of all the mountains and lakes she passed along the way. The means she chose of doing so was by stitching the images on her dress. By the time they reached a suitable place to settle, her clothing was covered with embroidered designs. This, it's said, was the origin of Miao embroidery. As the story tells us, the designs in Miao embroidery are closely related to the natural world and daily life. The Miao people have a special fondness for nature. So, as well as depicting their daily farming and work activities, they copy birds, flowers, mountains, and grass onto their clothing. Over the years, the embroidery of the Miao people has become a written record of their life. The stitches are like characters which, when many of them are combined, become a record of their history, their collected wisdom, and the knowledge passed down from their ancestors.

programme.title: Exploring the Folklore of Chongqing
programme.desc: Exploring the Folklore of Chongqing delves into the historical origins and cultural background of Fengdu Ghost City, and also features the Zhongyuan Festival celebrations and ancestor - worshipping rituals held here. These activities reflect the local people's positive and optimistic outlook on life and death, as well as the great importance they attach to their ancestors, families and family traditions.

programme.title: Aerial China IV: Hong Kong
programme.desc: Hong Kong, a city of skyscrapers positively pulsing with financial energy, the legendary Pearl of the Orient. But there’s another side to that great city - the nighttime romance of Victoria Harbour, islands frozen in time for hundreds of millions of years, a metropolis constantly changing and transforming itself. Join us for the ultimate bird’s eyes of Hong Kong!

programme.title: Shunde's Waterways: where business smarts meet everyday life
programme.desc: Shunde, a district in Guangdong Province, lies in the Pearl River Delta, north of Hong Kong - a water-rich region that lives by water and knows how to turn it into opportunity. Once, boats carried silk down its canals from small villages, building a legacy of trade. Today, Xiangyunsha (gambiered Canton gauze) is a global fashion icon, and historic spots like Mingshi Garden draw tourists and locals alike. With water as their muse and grit as their guide, Shunde folks keep business thriving while making life sweeter - that's the quiet wisdom flowing through their rivers. Now, two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia are setting out to explore more with the locals...

programme.title: Morning Tea in Wuzhong
programme.desc: This documentary explores Wuzhong's unique morning tea culture from an international perspective. Through compelling stories, it showcases the city’s charming landscapes, inclusive atmosphere and the everyday lives of its residents.

programme.title: Gourmets Alive II Ep.5
programme.desc: Literati such as Lu You, Li Yu, Yuan Mei, and Wang Zengqi take center stage as we explore their worlds and works through the flavors and cuisine of daily life.

programme.title: From Farm to Table (China-France Season) Ep.3
programme.desc: Set against the backdrop of the 60th anniversary of Sino-French diplomatic relations, this program focuses on the full-chain coordination mechanism that brings food from French farms to Chinese tables, capturing the collision and fusion of two great food cultures.

programme.title: Foodwise: Xilingol
programme.desc: The Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region is located in the northern part of China, stretching from northeast to southwest side. In Xilin Gol, the horses, sheep and cows could be found every where. The local cuisines here are so attractive to the tourists, such as the roasted lamb is a traditional local dish. And the fired stone fried lamb is so hard to find if you are not traveling to Inner Mongolia. Have you ever tried salted milk tea? Just join in this visual trip！

programme.title: Foodwise: The Herbal Way of Life
programme.desc: 'Medicine tonic is not as good as food tonic' - this Chinese saying is a core principle of Traditional Chinese Medicine. It is believed that the right diet and nourishment can cure and reverse the effects of disease, hence considered an inevitable source of natural health preservation. In this Foodwise episode, our hosts Tianran He and Eva May explore this ancient concept of medicine food homology as they taste their way through different herbs, chat to experts of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and visit venues that combine conventional principles with modern ideas. Dive deep into the origin of TCM with us as we learn about the harmony between man and nature and its application in modern functional foods!

programme.title: China Bound: Chengdu
programme.desc: Tianran spends 3 days in Chengdu, the capital of Sichuan Province and UNESCO's first City of Gastronomy. He dives deep into Chengdu culture, exploring the infamous "mala" numbing and spicy flavors of Sichuanese street food and hotpot, and visiting historical attractions like Wuhou Shrine, Du Fu's Thatched Cottage, and the Jinsha Site Museum, which houses exquisite relics from a 3,000-year-old kingdom uncovered beneath the streets of Chengdu. Of course, no visit to this city is complete without seeing giant pandas and enjoying a cup of tea while getting your ears cleaned in the iconic People's Park. After all, when in Chengdu, do as the locals do.

Trekking into the far-flung pastoral corners of the plateau, we listened closely to the stories behind the hurdles and hopes of pastoral life and development.

programme.desc: Shunde, a gastronomic gem in the Pearl River Delta, neighboring Hong Kong, uses masterful craft and sincere heart to transform local treasures - from crispy fish skin to fried milk - into culinary wonders. Now, two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia, are setting out to taste the flavors and feel the warmth of Shunde's countryside with the locals.

programme.title: A Canopy of Umbrellas, a Sichuan Serenade
programme.desc: The documentary "A Canopy of Umbrellas, a Sichuan Serenade" follows a father and son as they carry forward the centuries-old craft of making Luzhou oil-paper umbrellas. Each umbrella tells a story - not only of skill, but of family and cultural resilience. As part of CGTN's original series "Next Stop: China," this episode journeys into the lush bamboo forests of Sichuan, where traditional craftsmanship finds new life in the modern world.

programme.title: Find Me Beyond the Kitchen Ep.2
programme.desc: This film follows four culinary artists: a Yunnan-based chef specializing in plant-based cuisine; a Tibetan baker; a Chinese-Western fusion pastry chef; and an artist/restaurant owner. These are true masters of the kitchen, honoring their time-honored cuisines while staying true to their original visions.

programme.title: Gourmets Alive II Ep.7
programme.desc: Literati such as Lu You, Li Yu, Yuan Mei, and Wang Zengqi take center stage as we explore their worlds and works through the flavors and cuisine of daily life.

programme.desc: The first season of the "Wandering the World" series follows a traveler across six of China's greatest grasslands, revealing the natural beauty of their epic landscapes and the distinctive lives of the people who inhabit them.

programme.title: Mount Wutai, Embracing the Wonders of Nature
programme.desc: Mount Wutai, in the northeastern part of Shanxi Province, is one of the Four Great Buddhist Mountains of China. It is a magnet for tourists, who are drawn here not only by its profound Buddhist cultural heritage, but also by the spectacular natural scenery. Mount Wutai is noted for its unique topography, marked by five flattened peaks. Hence the name "Wutai," or "Five Terraces." The five, each with its own characteristics and distinct shape, are Wanghai East Peak, Guayue West Peak, Jinxiu South Peak, Yedou North Peak, and Cuiyan Central Peak. Soaring into the clouds, together they resemble a magnificent work crafted by nature.

programme.title: The Datong Motorcycle Diaries
programme.desc: In this Episode, we explore dragon walls in Datong, the City of Dragon Walls, to create a new tourist trail. The host then rides a motorcycle along Datong's Great Wall, presenting local culture and scenic spots along the way.

programme.title: Bird's-eye China Ep.1
programme.desc: Unfolding between the Kunlun, Altai and Tianshan ranges, cradling two vast basins, lies a beautiful land: Xinjiang. Join us on an aerial journey as we ascend the Tianshan to reveal the life-giving secrets of its crystal clear waters, before touching the summit of Bogda Peak, towering 5 km above sea-level, and gliding over the glittering, gem-like Tianchi Lake and the boundless grasslands that extend far beyond what even a bird's eye can see into the west...

programme.title: Celebrating Shuyang Festival in the Longji Rice Terraces
programme.desc: The Longji Rice Terraces in Guangxi are renowned for their magnificent scenery and unique cultural value. Julian Waghann from the United States and Eliza Arce from the Philippines arrived at the cloud-wrapped Longji Rice Terraces to take part in the most solemn annual farming festival: the Shuyang Festival. From the moment they stepped onto the terraces, they walked along the narrow ridges, joined the ancient seedling-combing ritual, sampled distinctive local cuisine, and lifted torches at nightfall to parade and pray with the villagers through the shimmering paddies. Through these vivid scenes, they gradually came to understand the centuries-old symbiotic relationship between the local people and the terraces. The Longji Rice Terraces are not just a breathtaking agricultural panorama - they are a mountain lifestyle and a cultural experience that still breathes today.

programme.title: Shared Roots in Wrestling
programme.desc: The documentary "Shared Roots in Wrestling" follows a young wrestler from Tianjin as he journeys to Inner Mongolia to explore the shared heritage of Chinese-style wrestling and Bökh, the region's national wrestling tradition. Part of CGTN's original series "Next Stop: China," this episode uncovers how strength, skill, and resilience connect athletes across city streets and endless grasslands, carrying forward a legacy that transcends geography and generations.

programme.title: China Bound: Tianjin
programme.desc: Tianran He explores the vibrant port city of Tianjin. Strolling through its historic quarters, he discovers how old buildings are being preserved and revitalized, and savors the rich flavors of authentic Tianjin cuisine. To work off the calories, he joins energetic retirees for a morning workout in the park, then takes in the lively nightlife along the banks of the Haihe River. From folk handicrafts on Ancient Culture Street to the National Maritime Museum and an aircraft carrier theme park, Tianran discovers that Tianjin is a truly multifacted city.

programme.title: China's Green Revolution Ep.2
programme.desc: China's ecological civilization and achievements are celebrated through stories of green development, like the Saihanba and Kubuqi restoration projects.

programme.title: Between Heaven and Earth : Traveling Through Grasslands Ep.6
programme.desc: The first season of the "Wandering the World" series follows a traveler across six of China's greatest grasslands, revealing the natural beauty of their epic landscapes and the distinctive lives of the people who inhabit them.

programme.title: Gulangyu Island
programme.desc: Gulangyu Island is famous for its exotic architecture. As a key trade port in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, it was a gathering point for merchants and diplomats from all over the world. This led to a variety of architectural styles being adopted on the island, including a fusion of Chinese and Western designs, as well as some typical of the Chaozhou region. These buildings, mostly over 100 years old, stand witness to China's reconnection with the outside world.

programme.title: Nature's Bounty
programme.desc: In this episode, we start from hiking up volcanoes in Datong. There is a large volcanic cluster with over 30 cones. Then we come to the Hanging Temple - a 1,500-year-old monastery clutching at a cliff of Mount Hengshan. Join us for an adrenaline-pumping adventure!

programme.title: Bird's-eye China Ep.2
programme.desc: Heilongjiang, China's northernmost province, is home to a veritable sea of trees, a forest forged by the Greater and Lesser Khingan Ranges. Beginning our Odyssey at its very northern extremity - a land of snowy Arctic snowscape and dazzling rime-frosts that's a paradise for winter-sports daredevils - we then head for Harbin and its spectacular ice festival in pursuit of some unique snowy adventures...

programme.title: The secret of the 'Long Hair' village
programme.desc: For the Red Yao women of Guangxi, southern China, hair is far more than a mark of beauty - it's a living narrative of identity, lineage, and nature. Each stage of life is reflected in how they wear it, carrying the memory of their families and the wisdom of their ancestors. Their time-honored rice-water hair care ritual is not just a beauty secret - it's a thread connecting generations, preserving ecological knowledge passed down through centuries. Join CGTN host Julian Waghann and Filipina singer Eliza Arce as they step into Huangluo Yao Village, known as the "World's Longest Hair Village," to uncover the stories and traditions behind the Red Yao's legendary long hair.

programme.title: Harmony Keepers: Guardians of Tibetan antelopes
programme.desc: This documentary series pays tribute to the guardians of China's rare wildlife and their habitats. Through the lens of ecological protection and preservation, the series features four iconic protected species in China: the Tibetan antelope, milu deer, black-necked cranes, and golden snub-nosed monkeys.

Beginning our Odyssey at its very northern extremity - a land of snowy Arctic snowscape and dazzling rime-frosts that's a paradise for winter-sports daredevils - we then head for Harbin and its spectacular ice festival in pursuit of some unique snowy adventures...

programme.title: The secret of the 'Long Hair' village
programme.desc: For the Red Yao women of Guangxi, southern China, hair is far more than a mark of beauty - it's a living narrative of identity, lineage, and nature. Each stage of life is reflected in how they wear it, carrying the memory of their families and the wisdom of their ancestors. Their time-honored rice-water hair care ritual is not just a beauty secret - it's a thread connecting generations, preserving ecological knowledge passed down through centuries. Join CGTN host Julian Waghann and Filipina singer Eliza Arce as they step into Huangluo Yao Village, known as the "World's Longest Hair Village," to uncover the stories and traditions behind the Red Yao's legendary long hair.

programme.title: Harmony Keepers: Guardians of Tibetan antelopes
programme.desc: This documentary series pays tribute to the guardians of China's rare wildlife and their habitats. Through the lens of ecological protection and preservation, the series features four iconic protected species in China: the Tibetan antelope, milu deer, black-necked cranes, and golden snub-nosed monkeys.

programme.title: Find Me Beyond the Kitchen Ep.3
programme.desc: This film follows four culinary artists: a Yunnan-based chef specializing in plant-based cuisine; a Tibetan baker; a Chinese-Western fusion pastry chef; and an artist/restaurant owner. These are true masters of the kitchen, honoring their time-honored cuisines while staying true to their original visions.

programme.title: Gourmets Alive II Ep.8
programme.desc: Literati such as Lu You, Li Yu, Yuan Mei, and Wang Zengqi take center stage as we explore their worlds and works through the flavors and cuisine of daily life.

programme.title: From Farm to Table (China-France Season) Ep.6
programme.desc: Set against the backdrop of the 60th anniversary of Sino-French diplomatic relations, this program focuses on the full-chain coordination mechanism that brings food from French farms to Chinese tables, capturing the collision and fusion of two great food cultures.

programme.title: Sweet Planet Ep.2
programme.desc: From China to France, America to India, and beyond - throughout human history, confectionery and desserts have united the world's shared sweet tooth, bringing hope and connection.

programme.title: China Bound: Tianjin
programme.desc: Tianran He explores the vibrant port city of Tianjin. Strolling through its historic quarters, he discovers how old buildings are being preserved and revitalized, and savors the rich flavors of authentic Tianjin cuisine. To work off the calories, he joins energetic retirees for a morning workout in the park, then takes in the lively nightlife along the banks of the Haihe River. From folk handicrafts on Ancient Culture Street to the National Maritime Museum and an aircraft carrier theme park, Tianran discovers that Tianjin is a truly multifacted city.

programme.title: China's Green Revolution Ep.2
programme.desc: China's ecological civilization and achievements are celebrated through stories of green development, like the Saihanba and Kubuqi restoration projects.

programme.title: Between Heaven and Earth : Traveling Through Grasslands Ep.6
programme.desc: The first season of the "Wandering the World" series follows a traveler across six of China's greatest grasslands, revealing the natural beauty of their epic landscapes and the distinctive lives of the people who inhabit them.

programme.title: Gulangyu Island
programme.desc: Gulangyu Island is famous for its exotic architecture. As a key trade port in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, it was a gathering point for merchants and diplomats from all over the world. This led to a variety of architectural styles being adopted on the island, including a fusion of Chinese and Western designs, as well as some typical of the Chaozhou region. These buildings, mostly over 100 years old, stand witness to China's reconnection with the outside world.

programme.title: Nature's Bounty
programme.desc: In this episode, we start from hiking up volcanoes in Datong. There is a large volcanic cluster with over 30 cones. Then we come to the Hanging Temple - a 1,500-year-old monastery clutching at a cliff of Mount Hengshan. Join us for an adrenaline-pumping adventure!

programme.title: Sweet Planet Ep.3
programme.desc: From China to France, America to India, and beyond - throughout human history, confectionery and desserts have united the world's shared sweet tooth, bringing hope and connection.

programme.title: China Bound: Wuhan
programme.desc: Tianran He visits Wuhan, a megacity at the crossroads of central China. From experiencing its vibrant breakfast culture and iconic dishes like hot dry noodles to exploring the lakes and hills of the expansive East Lake, as well as historic districts that showcase a blend of Chinese and Western architecture, Tianran uncovers why Wuhan has been a pivotal city in Chinese history for centuries. Finally, he relives some of these moments through immersive theater performances set amongst historic buildings and aboard a steamship cruising the Yangtze River.

programme.title: China's Green Revolution Ep.3
programme.desc: China's ecological civilization and achievements are celebrated through stories of green development, like the Saihanba and Kubuqi restoration projects.

programme.title: Between Heaven and Earth : Traveling Through Grasslands Ep.7
programme.desc: The first season of the "Wandering the World" series follows a traveler across six of China's greatest grasslands, revealing the natural beauty of their epic landscapes and the distinctive lives of the people who inhabit them.

programme.title: Jingmai Wanderings: A Symphony of Humans and Tea
programme.desc: As a UNESCO World Heritage site, Mount Jingmai embodies the ecological wisdom of forest-tea symbiosis and the rich cultural diversity of its ethnic communities. It plays a vital role in biodiversity conservation and the preservation of traditional tea culture. This episode follows the stories of representative individuals to explore three key themes - heritage preservation, ecological sustainability, and youth empowerment - revealing the unique charm and sustainable development model of Mount Jingmai.

programme.title: Navigating the Hills of Chongqing
programme.desc: This episode explores the transportation ingenuity of Chongqing, the Fog City. Surrounded by mountains and rivers, this megacity solves topographic challenges with the Yangtze River Cableway, Asia's second-longest escalator, and a train passing through a building. From the dock culture at the confluence of two rivers to a logistics hub linking China and Europe, witness its transformation from an inland town to an economic center via the Go West policy.

programme.title: Bird's-eye China Ep.3
programme.desc: Hainan- the anchor-point of China's southern frontier, its islands custodians of the vast South China Sea! And perhaps nothing embodies the allure of the oceanic wonderland more than the limpid waters of Sansha. From volcanic northern shores to cutting-edge modern cities, join us on coastal journey dotted with historic lighthouses illuminating a fascinating past and guiding the way to a promising future...

programme.title: Clothing woven in the mountains
programme.desc: In Longsheng, southern China, ethnic communities have lived for generations among the same mountains and rivers. The landscape of terraced fields stretches across the valleys, carrying layered cultural memories. In this episode, CGTN host Julian Waghann and Filipino singer Eliza Arce travel to Huangluo Yao Village. Beginning with the Red Yao tradition of sun-drying clothes, they explore the colours, craftsmanship, and everyday wisdom woven into these garments. Their journey culminates in a vibrant bonfire gathering, where different communities come together in celebration.

programme.title: Xuancheng: Haven of Poetry
programme.desc: This episode explores Xuancheng, Anhui. The presenter visits the Yangtze Alligator Reserve, enjoys Huaguxi opera, and explores the ancient Shuidong Town. She experiences shadow‑puppetry and tours a century‑old, Gothic-style Catholic church. Later she visits the majestic Xietiao Tower, tours a heritage distillery, and climbs the fabled Mount Jingting, tasting local tea to savour Xuancheng's rich natural and cultural heritage.

programme.title: Dance of Heroes
programme.desc: In this episode, our host "Uncle Hanzi" travels to Chaonan in Shantou to explore the story of a family devoted to the tradition of Yingge dance. Centered around inheritor Hong Shaohua, the story unfolds through his father's dedication, his daughter's passion, and his apprentices'enthusiasm - showcasing how this centuries - old folk art continues to thrive in the modern world.

programme.title: Bird's-eye China Ep.4
programme.desc: Shaanxi, almost right in the middle of China, is a true land of contrasts. South of the Qinling Mountains that divide the province, the terrain has all the allure of south China, while north of this great dividing range lies the Guanzhong Plain and the austere and otherworldly Loess Plateau. Join us for a journey into a province that presents two equally beautiful and fascinating faces to the world!

programme.title: Into Guilin's landscapes: A new way to experience rural China
programme.desc: Guilin in south China's Guangxi region has long been celebrated for its breathtaking karst landscapes. Today, more and more travelers are discovering the region in a different way. Instead of simply admiring the scenery, they immerse themselves in it through cycling, hiking, bamboo rafting or via ferrata, experiencing the countryside from a new perspective. Supported by convenient transport links and a thriving outdoor recreation industry, Yangshuo County in Guilin is emerging as a global magnet where nature, culture and local life converge. Join CGTN host Julian Waghann and Filipina singer Eliza Arce as they explore Yangshuo through a variety of outdoor adventures.

programme.desc: Shaanxi, almost right in the middle of China, is a true land of contrasts. programme.title: Into Guilin's landscapes: A new way to experience rural China
programme.desc: Guilin in south China's Guangxi region has long been celebrated for its breathtaking karst landscapes. Today, more and more travelers are discovering the region in a different way. Instead of simply admiring the scenery, they immerse themselves in it through cycling, hiking, bamboo rafting or via ferrata, experiencing the countryside from a new perspective. Supported by convenient transport links and a thriving outdoor recreation industry, Yangshuo County in Guilin is emerging as a global magnet where nature, culture and local life converge. Join CGTN host Julian Waghann and Filipina singer Eliza Arce as they explore Yangshuo through a variety of outdoor adventures.

programme.title: Back to the Land: Exploring new life in rural China
programme.desc: When we think of the countryside, what colour comes to mind? The answer lies in Wuxin - Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal and Water - an ancient rhythm that still pulses beneath China's landscapes. In this programme, we explore how the colours of Wuxing come to life through the traditions of China's ethnic minority groups. From Lugu Lake's matrilineal water world and the metal-hued fire of the Yi Torch Festival, to Dali's earth-driven crafts, Guizhou's wooden Dong dwellings, and the volcanic winds of Inner Mongolia's new nomadic life - the Five Elements guide the stories of people reconnecting with land, culture and community.

programme.title: Bird's-eye China Ep.5
programme.desc: Guarded by mountains in southeast China, Jiangxi channels rivers into Poyang Lake---the Yangtze's vital link. Starting from Mount Lu's misty slopes, watch and marvel as northern plains transition into an undulating land of hills and basins...

programme.title: Ride the trails, unlock Chongli's rhythm
programme.desc: Chongli in Zhangjiakou, north China's Hebei Province, first made its name with Winter Olympic ski runs. Now, with cool summers and a wealth of outdoor activities, this mountain town is writing a new summer chapter. CGTN host Julian Waghann and Mexican traveler Juan Carlos Cheang Guzman came to explore. They tried mountain biking and discovered the sustainable model of "winter skiing, summer cycling." At an ultra-trail race, runners pressed forward through pouring rain, their headlamps flickering like stars across the night. The Olympics may have ended, but the venues are far from dormant. They power new vitality for Chongli's all-season sports and cultural tourism.

programme.title: Korela Fortress Museum, Russia
programme.desc: 4K Documentary on Korela Fortress Museum, RussiaAt 160 km from St. Petersburg, there is a small town in northern Russia: Priozersk. Here, on the picturesque banks of the Vuoksa River's mouth and Lake Ladoga, stands the Korela Fortress Museum. Medieval Korela was the most northwestern city of Russia on the Vuoksa River island and served to protect against the Swedes' attack. The foundation date of the Korela Fortress is considered to be 1310. This Fortress is the only surviving Swedish bastion-type Fortress in Russia, on which unique buildings of 6-8 centuries are located: Lars Torstenson's Round Gate Tower, the Old Arsenal, the Powder Magazine, and the Suvorov Arsenal. Initially, the buildings of the Fortress were wooden, but numerous fires destroyed them. Over three centuries, the defensive structure was rebuilt and fortified many times. In the 15th century, Korela occupied an area of 6 thousand square meters, consisted of hundreds of log houses, and its population was more than 300 people. The people of the city were engaged in agriculture and fishing and also professed Christianity.By the sixteenth century, the Fortress acquired the form that has survived to this day. In the eighteenth century, the defense served as a prison for essential state criminals. The round gate tower of Lars Torstenson, located at the junction of the north-west and south-west curtains, is a Swedish building. The time of its construction dates back to 1583-1585. In plan, the tower has an almost circular shape, slightly elongated in the western and eastern directions. During its existence, the Fortress has changed more than one name. ""Korela"" repeatedly passed from Sweden to Russia and back and later belonged to Finland. Each country called this place differently. The original name ""Korela"" came from the name of a tribe that once lived in this area. It's interesting to know that until 19-century Korela was located on an island washed on both sides by the Vuoksa river. Due to its favorable geographic location, the Fortress was practically impregnable.

programme.title: Car History
programme.desc: The Jaguar E-Type is a century-old sports car whose look still quickens the pulse today. Those responsible at Jaguar waited almost 40 years before they dared to build a successor to one of the most beautiful cars in the world.

programme.title: Car History
programme.desc: The early history of sports car manufacturer Lamborghini was shaped by the rivalry between tractor manufacturer Ferruccio Lamborghini and Enzo Ferrari. Over the years, the brand launched some of the most striking sports cars in the world.

programme.title: Car History
programme.desc: The 1960s and 1970s were golden years for Opel. Ascona, Manta, Rekord and GT, an Opel was more than just a car, and the company built one classic after another. Today, these car models are all icons.

programme.title: Car History
programme.desc: Since the 1950s, the Mercedes-Benz S-Class has set the standard in the luxury class. The status model of the rich, famous and powerful prevails against crises, social change and all competitors.

programme.title: Car History
programme.desc: The BMW 3 Series is the epitome of a sports saloon. Since its debut in 1975, it has been the undisputed leader of the premium segment. It's a family saloon, a sports car, a tuning object and a racing car.

programme.title: Mercedes 300 SL Lightweight
programme.desc: An iconic racing car and one of only 29 ever built! We accompanied the Mercedes 300 SL 'lightweight' on its premiere drive at the Mille Miglia.

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: The sound of the McLaren 720S Spider is that of an uncompromising driving machine. Also: the F-Pace SVR makes a rather sophisticated impression. And: is the Porsche Cayenne coupe's higher price justifiable compared to the regular model?

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: How much power is there in the Limited Edition of the Seat Cupra Ateca? Also: are the Porsche 718 Boxster and the Cayman in the GTS version an alternative to the expensive 911? And: the exclusive preview of Audi's RS6 powerful station wagon.

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: Does the Skoda Enyaq Coupe RS iV live up to the famous "Rally Sport" abbreviation in its model designation as an e-car? And how does Mercedes-AMG manage without the brand's usual V8 sound in the EQE 53?

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: Two car brands turn their drive concepts upside down: for the first time since the 1980s, Maserati builds a mid-engine sports car. And Corvette's C8 with mid-engine instead of classic front-wheel drive redefines the American Dream.

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: We focus on premium-quality electric cars. The Mercedes EQS 450+ faces our test in the Swiss Alps. Plus: Is the Porsche Taycan Cross Turismo Turbo S the ultimate mobility all-purpose weapon? And: The Audi E-Tron GT from the same platform as the Taycan.

programme.title: Alpina B6
programme.desc: An Alpina is optically never intrusive. Understatement is the motto. One should not recognize at first glance, what potential is hidden under the bodywork. Huge spoilers are not used and neither are striking power domes. Any modifications serve the technical improvement, for example, optimized cooling and aerodynamics.

programme.title: Hook Down, Wheels Down
programme.desc: Produced in the early 1970s, "Hook Down, Wheels Down" was one of the most comprehensive (and expensive) films made by the U.S. Navy. It covers the history and development of the U.S. aircraft carrier, and does so through interviews with many of the men who made it happen. While dozens of aircraft carriers are featured, it is the USS John F. Kennedy (CV-67) that takes center stage -- and the material shot on her deck looks like it is right out of "Top Gun". There is wonderful flight op footage, great aerial flight footage, incredible WWII dog fightand bombing footage as well as endless aircraft carrier operational footage. Also shown in this film are very rare images of the first aircraft carrier USS Langley (CV-1) (formerly collier USS Jupiter AC-3). The follow on vessels are widely featured including USS Lexington (CV-3) and the USS Yorktown (CV-5) in the Battle of Coral Sea. Also featured: USS Saratoga (CV-2), USS Enterprise (CV-6), USS Hornet (CV-8), USS Wasp (CV-7), USS Ranger (CV-4), USS Yorktown (CV-5), USS Essex (CV-9), USS Guadalcanal (CVE-60), the British carrier HMS Furious, the destroyer USS Zeilin (DD-313), and many other warships. Various incidents are shown from Pearl Harbor, Midway, Coral Sea, the capture of the submarine U-505, the Marianas Turkey Shoot, the Doolittle Raid on Japan, and more. Includes interviews or appearances by many WWII naval aviators and aces including Wade McClusky, John Jay Courtney, Billy Mitchell, Gerald Bogen, Leslie Generes, John S. Thatch (of "Thatch Weave" fame), Ensign George Gay, David Campbell (whose Minsi III appears in the film), Edward "Butch" O'Hare, Charles Lindbergh, Glenn Curtiss, Clark Gable and Wallace Beery. Planes seen in the film include the Wright Brothers flier, biplanes, Lindbergh's Spirit of St. Louis, the NC-4 Flying Boat, Hellcat, Avenger, Corsair, Vindicator, Devastator, Wildcat, and Japanese Zero. Also seen in the film: dogfights, combat flying, the Washington Conference on battleships, the Panama Canal exercise of 1929, air mail service.

programme.title: Kia Sportage Exterior Design in Lunar Silver
programme.desc:
A number of new technologies optimize the precision and control of the chassis in a wide variety of weather and road conditions. The standard electronic damper control (Electronic Control Suspension, ECS) in the GT-line version increases comfort and safety thanks to the continuous damping control. The system reacts to body movements and steering inputs and changes the damping behavior at lightning speed in order to counteract the vehicle's diving, pitching and rolling movements when cornering. It also adjusts the damping force in the case of obstacles in order to cope with them as comfortably as possible and to reduce the influence of post-vibrations on the wheels.
A premiere for the Sportage is the “All-Terrain-Mode”, which will be available for the plug-in hybrid version with all-wheel drive. The system offers intelligent support when driving off-road or on snow by automatically optimizing the vehicle settings depending on the selected mode and thus helping the SUV to achieve maximum traction on muddy, sandy or snowy surfaces.

programme.title: The new Mercedes-Benz GLC AMG Line World Premiere Teaser
programme.desc:
The new GLC is immediately recognisable as a member of the Mercedes-Benz SUV family. Standard equipment includes the AVANTGARDE exterior with Chrome package including chrome window surrounds and a new, chrome-look simulated underguard. This adds striking design features and enhances the unique proportions of the vehicle. One of the defining design highlights of the GLC is the redesigned front end, with headlamps that connect directly to the radiator grille to emphasise the vehicle’s width, and the new radiator grille as part of the standard AVANTGARDE exterior, which now has a chrome surround and a sporty louvre in matt grey with chrome trim. The AMG Line has a radiator grille with Mercedes-Benz pattern.
The body design is characterised by a full, spanned surface design enriched with precisely shaped edges in the sides. These emphasise the proportions, accentuate the muscular wheel arches and create a balance between elegance and off-road performance. Wheel arch liners in the vehicle colour are available from the AMG Line upwards for the first time. These accentuate the sportiness of the AMG Line, as optional equipment in conjunction with mixed tyres. Also available as an optional extra are easy-entry running boards and, from the AMG Line upwards, a Night package.

programme.desc:
With the luxury saloon EQS and the sporty executive saloon EQE, Mercedes-Benz has entered a new, all-electric era in the upper market segments as well. The EQS SUV, the third model series with this architecture developed for electric vehicles, will soon follow. The SUV offers plenty of space, comfort and connectivity for up to seven passengers in its avant-garde, luxurious interior. Thanks to powerful electric motors, responsive 4MATIC all-wheel drive and an intelligent OFFROAD driving mode, the EQS SUV is also capable of tackling light terrain with ease.
The new EQS SUV shares the long wheelbase (3210 millimetres) with the EQS Saloon, but is over 20 centimetres higher. The dimensions in detail: 5125/1959/1718 millimetres (length/width/height). The interior dimensions benefit from these generous SUV dimensions and from the advantages of the purpose design tailored to the electric platform. The second row of seats can be electrically adjusted as standard. Up to four golf bags fit in the boot. A third row of seats with two additional individual seats and extensive comfort features for all passengers is available as an option.

programme.title: Colour change with the power of thought - The BMW iX Flow meets neuro-technology
programme.desc:
The Munich-based startup brainboost used the new and improved colour-changing effect in a one-off collaboration with the BMW Group at rad°hub aimed at raising awareness of mental health.
With the help of brainboost, the BMW iX Flow was connected directly to the brain of the rad°hub delegates using an electroencephalograph (EEG), which records the brain’s electrical activity. “The colour patterns of the BMW iX Flow react to brain activity and reflect the level of activity,” explains brainboost CEO Philipp Heiler. “Once the brain is at rest, the changes of patterns on the iX Flow also become calmer and more rhythmical.” A special animation was activated if delegates managed to maintain this state for several seconds. Thus, the participants were able to gradually calm and relax their brains under the guidance of the brainboost experts and with the help of neurofeedback via the iX Flow. This matures the knowledge of which strategies work best to specifically shut down one's own brain activity for relaxation, e.g. in everyday working life.

programme.title: New 2023 Range Rover Sport Design Reveal Film
programme.desc:
The New Range Rover Sport has made its global premiere with a dramatic world-first climb up a flooded dam spillway in Iceland.
The epic ascent saw New Range Rover Sport resist the surging torrent of water flowing down the ramp of the Karahnjukar Dam – the biggest of its kind in the world – at a rate of 750 tonnes per minute. A loss of traction risked plunging down the perilous 90m drop at the base of the spillway to the valley floor below.
The successful spillway ascent was screened for the first time at an exclusive launch event at Jaguar Land Rover’s Advanced Product Creation Centre at Gaydon, UK.
Official James Bond stunt driver Jessica Hawkins was behind the wheel as the New Range Rover Sport demonstrated its grip, traction, performance and composure, completing the latest in a series of challenges for Land Rover’s luxury performance SUV. Previous feats include a record-setting hill-climb at Pikes Peak, a first recorded crossing of the ‘Empty Quarter’ desert in the Arabian Peninsula and a first ascent of the 999 steps to Heaven’s Gate in China, in 2018.

programme.title: Hispano Suiza showcases its history in the Peralada Castle Museum
programme.desc:
The history of Hispano Suiza is showcased, for the very first time, in the Peralada Castle Museum (Girona, Spain) where visitors will be able to contemplate the past and present of the legendary car brand founded in 1904 by Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt.
The Hispano Suiza Room will close the usual tour of the Peralada Castle Museum. After years of researching to gather the largest number of pieces and objects related to its history, Hispano Suiza becomes part of this important collection. The Hispano Suiza exhibition encompasses a journey through various decades: from the beginning of the 20th century, when Hispano Suiza was founded, to the present day. After passing through a luxurious hall, the public will be able to visit a recreation of the offices of Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt, where countless business and technical ideas, emerged and took shape, turning Hispano Suiza into a point of reference, for luxury, comfort and technical solutions. In this area, the original painting 'Dame with a mink' by Ramon Casas takes pride of place: it was used as an illustration on the company's original shares.

programme.desc: Safety and customer satisfaction come first at Audi. They are part and parcel of the success of the company with the four rings. It is particularly visible in the new Audi A8: the forward-looking Digital Matrix LED headlights and digital OLED rear lights raise the customer experience to a whole new level: for the first time in any Audi model, light is completely digitized. programme.title: Mercedes-Benz DRIVE PILOT Sensors S-Class
programme.desc: The exact location of a Mercedes equipped with DRIVE PILOT is determined using a high-precision positioning system that is much more powerful than conventional GPS systems. In addition to the anonymised data collected by LiDAR, camera, radar and ultrasound sensors, a digital HD map provides a three-dimensional image of the road and the surroundings with information on road geometry, route characteristics, traffic signs and special traffic events (e.g. accidents or road works). This high-precision map differs from maps for navigation devices by, among other things, its higher accuracy in the centimetre rather than metre range and its detailed junction and route model. The map data is stored in backend data centres and updated constantly. Each vehicle also stores an image of this map information on board, constantly compares it with the backend data and updates the local dataset as required. All of this enables stable and accurate positioning through a representation of the surroundings that is independent of factors such as shadows or dirty sensors.

programme.title: Kia Sportage Exterior Design in Lunar Silver
programme.desc:
A number of new technologies optimize the precision and control of the chassis in a wide variety of weather and road conditions. The standard electronic damper control (Electronic Control Suspension, ECS) in the GT-line version increases comfort and safety thanks to the continuous damping control. The system reacts to body movements and steering inputs and changes the damping behavior at lightning speed in order to counteract the vehicle's diving, pitching and rolling movements when cornering. It also adjusts the damping force in the case of obstacles in order to cope with them as comfortably as possible and to reduce the influence of post-vibrations on the wheels.
A premiere for the Sportage is the “All-Terrain-Mode”, which will be available for the plug-in hybrid version with all-wheel drive. The system offers intelligent support when driving off-road or on snow by automatically optimizing the vehicle settings depending on the selected mode and thus helping the SUV to achieve maximum traction on muddy, sandy or snowy surfaces.

The interior dimensions benefit from these generous SUV dimensions and from the advantages of the purpose design tailored to the electric platform. The second row of seats can be electrically adjusted as standard. Up to four golf bags fit in the boot. A third row of seats with two additional individual seats and extensive comfort features for all passengers is available as an option.

programme.title: Colour change with the power of thought - The BMW iX Flow meets neuro-technology
programme.desc:
The Munich-based startup brainboost used the new and improved colour-changing effect in a one-off collaboration with the BMW Group at rad°hub aimed at raising awareness of mental health.
With the help of brainboost, the BMW iX Flow was connected directly to the brain of the rad°hub delegates using an electroencephalograph (EEG), which records the brain’s electrical activity. “The colour patterns of the BMW iX Flow react to brain activity and reflect the level of activity,” explains brainboost CEO Philipp Heiler. “Once the brain is at rest, the changes of patterns on the iX Flow also become calmer and more rhythmical.” A special animation was activated if delegates managed to maintain this state for several seconds. Thus, the participants were able to gradually calm and relax their brains under the guidance of the brainboost experts and with the help of neurofeedback via the iX Flow. This matures the knowledge of which strategies work best to specifically shut down one's own brain activity for relaxation, e.g. in everyday working life.

programme.title: New 2023 Range Rover Sport Design Reveal Film
programme.desc:
The New Range Rover Sport has made its global premiere with a dramatic world-first climb up a flooded dam spillway in Iceland.
The epic ascent saw New Range Rover Sport resist the surging torrent of water flowing down the ramp of the Karahnjukar Dam – the biggest of its kind in the world – at a rate of 750 tonnes per minute. A loss of traction risked plunging down the perilous 90m drop at the base of the spillway to the valley floor below.
The successful spillway ascent was screened for the first time at an exclusive launch event at Jaguar Land Rover’s Advanced Product Creation Centre at Gaydon, UK.
Official James Bond stunt driver Jessica Hawkins was behind the wheel as the New Range Rover Sport demonstrated its grip, traction, performance and composure, completing the latest in a series of challenges for Land Rover’s luxury performance SUV. Previous feats include a record-setting hill-climb at Pikes Peak, a first recorded crossing of the ‘Empty Quarter’ desert in the Arabian Peninsula and a first ascent of the 999 steps to Heaven’s Gate in China, in 2018.

programme.title: Hispano Suiza showcases its history in the Peralada Castle Museum
programme.desc:
The history of Hispano Suiza is showcased, for the very first time, in the Peralada Castle Museum (Girona, Spain) where visitors will be able to contemplate the past and present of the legendary car brand founded in 1904 by Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt.
The Hispano Suiza Room will close the usual tour of the Peralada Castle Museum. After years of researching to gather the largest number of pieces and objects related to its history, Hispano Suiza becomes part of this important collection. The Hispano Suiza exhibition encompasses a journey through various decades: from the beginning of the 20th century, when Hispano Suiza was founded, to the present day. After passing through a luxurious hall, the public will be able to visit a recreation of the offices of Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt, where countless business and technical ideas, emerged and took shape, turning Hispano Suiza into a point of reference, for luxury, comfort and technical solutions. In this area, the original painting 'Dame with a mink' by Ramon Casas takes pride of place: it was used as an illustration on the company's original shares.

programme.title: Mercedes-Benz DRIVE PILOT Sensors S-Class
programme.desc: The exact location of a Mercedes equipped with DRIVE PILOT is determined using a high-precision positioning system that is much more powerful than conventional GPS systems. In addition to the anonymised data collected by LiDAR, camera, radar and ultrasound sensors, a digital HD map provides a three-dimensional image of the road and the surroundings with information on road geometry, route characteristics, traffic signs and special traffic events (e.g. accidents or road works). This high-precision map differs from maps for navigation devices by, among other things, its higher accuracy in the centimetre rather than metre range and its detailed junction and route model. The map data is stored in backend data centres and updated constantly. Each vehicle also stores an image of this map information on board, constantly compares it with the backend data and updates the local dataset as required. All of this enables stable and accurate positioning through a representation of the surroundings that is independent of factors such as shadows or dirty sensors.

programme.title: Kia Sportage Exterior Design in Lunar Silver
programme.desc:
A number of new technologies optimize the precision and control of the chassis in a wide variety of weather and road conditions. The standard electronic damper control (Electronic Control Suspension, ECS) in the GT-line version increases comfort and safety thanks to the continuous damping control. The system reacts to body movements and steering inputs and changes the damping behavior at lightning speed in order to counteract the vehicle's diving, pitching and rolling movements when cornering. It also adjusts the damping force in the case of obstacles in order to cope with them as comfortably as possible and to reduce the influence of post-vibrations on the wheels.
A premiere for the Sportage is the “All-Terrain-Mode”, which will be available for the plug-in hybrid version with all-wheel drive. The system offers intelligent support when driving off-road or on snow by automatically optimizing the vehicle settings depending on the selected mode and thus helping the SUV to achieve maximum traction on muddy, sandy or snowy surfaces.

Subject to a limited production run for the first twelve months of orders, it combines many of the most desirable options available for the car with a package of eye-catching details found only on Bentley First Editions.
First Edition badging can be seen to the exterior of the car – a theme that extends inside, with badging on the veneered fascia, as well as embroidery on the seats. Unique First Edition contrast stitching and embroidery adorns the seats and, depending on the choice of veneers, handcrafted metal overlays just 0.075 mm thick can be applied to the fascia and waistrails in the front and the rear door veneer.
The First Edition offers elegant and timeless design, focusing on maximum comfort and well-being. This specifically tailored specification includes a unique 22” ten-spoke directional wheel and bright lower bumper grilles. Other additional features as standard include unique quilted seats, mood lighting, a heated steering wheel, and increased driver’s assistance aids. Attention to detail is clear, from the badging that identifies the car to the jewelled caps on the fuel and oil fillers.

programme.title: New 2023 Range Rover Sport Design Reveal Film
programme.desc:
The New Range Rover Sport has made its global premiere with a dramatic world-first climb up a flooded dam spillway in Iceland.
The epic ascent saw New Range Rover Sport resist the surging torrent of water flowing down the ramp of the Karahnjukar Dam – the biggest of its kind in the world – at a rate of 750 tonnes per minute. A loss of traction risked plunging down the perilous 90m drop at the base of the spillway to the valley floor below.
The successful spillway ascent was screened for the first time at an exclusive launch event at Jaguar Land Rover’s Advanced Product Creation Centre at Gaydon, UK.
Official James Bond stunt driver Jessica Hawkins was behind the wheel as the New Range Rover Sport demonstrated its grip, traction, performance and composure, completing the latest in a series of challenges for Land Rover’s luxury performance SUV. Previous feats include a record-setting hill-climb at Pikes Peak, a first recorded crossing of the ‘Empty Quarter’ desert in the Arabian Peninsula and a first ascent of the 999 steps to Heaven’s Gate in China, in 2018.

programme.title: Hispano Suiza showcases its history in the Peralada Castle Museum
programme.desc:
The history of Hispano Suiza is showcased, for the very first time, in the Peralada Castle Museum (Girona, Spain) where visitors will be able to contemplate the past and present of the legendary car brand founded in 1904 by Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt.
The Hispano Suiza Room will close the usual tour of the Peralada Castle Museum. After years of researching to gather the largest number of pieces and objects related to its history, Hispano Suiza becomes part of this important collection. The Hispano Suiza exhibition encompasses a journey through various decades: from the beginning of the 20th century, when Hispano Suiza was founded, to the present day. After passing through a luxurious hall, the public will be able to visit a recreation of the offices of Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt, where countless business and technical ideas, emerged and took shape, turning Hispano Suiza into a point of reference, for luxury, comfort and technical solutions. In this area, the original painting 'Dame with a mink' by Ramon Casas takes pride of place: it was used as an illustration on the company's original shares.

programme.title: TechDay Digital Light - Digital Future Lighting
programme.desc: Safety and customer satisfaction come first at Audi. They are part and parcel of the success of the company with the four rings. In that context, light technology is steadily growing more important and creating a wider range of possibilities and perspectives, from added safety for the driver, to external communication and individualization. Systematic light digitization is making all of this possible. It is particularly visible in the new Audi A8: the forward-looking Digital Matrix LED headlights and digital OLED rear lights raise the customer experience to a whole new level: for the first time in any Audi model, light is completely digitized. The car can be individualized even further through its digital OLED rear lights. The Digital Matrix LED headlights also include three new functions: advanced traffic information, a lane light with direction indicator lights on highways, and an orientation light on country roads. These features not only demonstrate Audi’s “Vorsprung durch Technik,” they also add value.

programme.title: Mercedes-Benz DRIVE PILOT Sensors S-Class
programme.desc: The exact location of a Mercedes equipped with DRIVE PILOT is determined using a high-precision positioning system that is much more powerful than conventional GPS systems. In addition to the anonymised data collected by LiDAR, camera, radar and ultrasound sensors, a digital HD map provides a three-dimensional image of the road and the surroundings with information on road geometry, route characteristics, traffic signs and special traffic events (e.g. accidents or road works). This high-precision map differs from maps for navigation devices by, among other things, its higher accuracy in the centimetre rather than metre range and its detailed junction and route model. The map data is stored in backend data centres and updated constantly. Each vehicle also stores an image of this map information on board, constantly compares it with the backend data and updates the local dataset as required. All of this enables stable and accurate positioning through a representation of the surroundings that is independent of factors such as shadows or dirty sensors.

programme.title: Kia Sportage Exterior Design in Lunar Silver
programme.desc:
A number of new technologies optimize the precision and control of the chassis in a wide variety of weather and road conditions. The standard electronic damper control (Electronic Control Suspension, ECS) in the GT-line version increases comfort and safety thanks to the continuous damping control. The system reacts to body movements and steering inputs and changes the damping behavior at lightning speed in order to counteract the vehicle's diving, pitching and rolling movements when cornering. It also adjusts the damping force in the case of obstacles in order to cope with them as comfortably as possible and to reduce the influence of post-vibrations on the wheels.
A premiere for the Sportage is the “All-Terrain-Mode”, which will be available for the plug-in hybrid version with all-wheel drive. The system offers intelligent support when driving off-road or on snow by automatically optimizing the vehicle settings depending on the selected mode and thus helping the SUV to achieve maximum traction on muddy, sandy or snowy surfaces.

The new GLC is immediately recognisable as a member of the Mercedes-Benz SUV family. Standard equipment includes the AVANTGARDE exterior with Chrome package including chrome window surrounds and a new, chrome-look simulated underguard. One of the defining design highlights of the GLC is the redesigned front end, with headlamps that connect directly to the radiator grille to emphasise the vehicle’s width, and the new radiator grille as part of the standard AVANTGARDE exterior, which now has a chrome surround and a sporty louvre in matt grey with chrome trim. The body design is characterised by a full, spanned surface design enriched with precisely shaped edges in the sides. These emphasise the proportions, accentuate the muscular wheel arches and create a balance between elegance and off-road performance. Wheel arch liners in the vehicle colour are available from the AMG Line upwards for the first time. These accentuate the sportiness of the AMG Line, as optional equipment in conjunction with mixed tyres. Also available as an optional extra are easy-entry running boards and, from the AMG Line upwards, a Night package.

programme.desc:
With the luxury saloon EQS and the sporty executive saloon EQE, Mercedes-Benz has entered a new, all-electric era in the upper market segments as well. The EQS SUV, the third model series with this architecture developed for electric vehicles, will soon follow. The SUV offers plenty of space, comfort and connectivity for up to seven passengers in its avant-garde, luxurious interior. Thanks to powerful electric motors, responsive 4MATIC all-wheel drive and an intelligent OFFROAD driving mode, the EQS SUV is also capable of tackling light terrain with ease.
The new EQS SUV shares the long wheelbase (3210 millimetres) with the EQS Saloon, but is over 20 centimetres higher. The dimensions in detail: 5125/1959/1718 millimetres (length/width/height). The interior dimensions benefit from these generous SUV dimensions and from the advantages of the purpose design tailored to the electric platform. The second row of seats can be electrically adjusted as standard. Up to four golf bags fit in the boot. A third row of seats with two additional individual seats and extensive comfort features for all passengers is available as an option.

programme.title: Colour change with the power of thought - The BMW iX Flow meets neuro-technology
programme.desc:
The Munich-based startup brainboost used the new and improved colour-changing effect in a one-off collaboration with the BMW Group at rad°hub aimed at raising awareness of mental health.
With the help of brainboost, the BMW iX Flow was connected directly to the brain of the rad°hub delegates using an electroencephalograph (EEG), which records the brain’s electrical activity. “The colour patterns of the BMW iX Flow react to brain activity and reflect the level of activity,” explains brainboost CEO Philipp Heiler. “Once the brain is at rest, the changes of patterns on the iX Flow also become calmer and more rhythmical.” A special animation was activated if delegates managed to maintain this state for several seconds. Thus, the participants were able to gradually calm and relax their brains under the guidance of the brainboost experts and with the help of neurofeedback via the iX Flow. This matures the knowledge of which strategies work best to specifically shut down one's own brain activity for relaxation, e.g. in everyday working life.

programme.title: The Secret Lives of Big Cats - S01:E01 - The Secret Lives of Tigers
programme.desc: Big cat populations are shrinking fast, but now we have the means to view them in more detail than ever. Siberian tigers are the largest of all cats. In historic times, the tiger's range was vast, covering much of Asia. Over the last century, they've experienced an almost total population crash, and at least 97% of those tigers have gone.

programme.title: The Secret Lives of Big Cats - S01:E02 - The Secret Lives of Snow Leopards
programme.desc: Big cat populations are shrinking fast, but now we have the means to view them in more detail than ever. Often referred to as the gray ghost or ghost of the mountains, this animal's rarity and elusiveness was legendary. In the past, it was known as the ounce, but today we've settled on the name snow leopard.

programme.title: The Secret Lives of Big Cats - S01:E03 - The Secret Lives of Pumas
programme.desc: Big cat populations are shrinking fast, but now we have the means to view them in more detail than ever. Pumas are also known by the names of cougar or mountain lion. However, these cats are only distantly related to lions. They're much more closely related to cheetahs. programme.title: Breakthrough - S01:E83 - The Great Seaweed Invasion
programme.desc: A giant mass of floating seaweed is invading popular beaches in the US and Caribbean!

programme.title: Breakthrough - S01:E92 - Superpredators
programme.desc: For thousands—or even millions—of years, they ruled the food chain. And they still fascinate us. Creatures synonymous with the hunt: Saber Teeth, Mega Jaws, even a Tyrant King. How did they win evolution’s race—and what brought their reign to an end?

programme.title: Breakthrough - S01:E49 - Flight of the Dragon Mission Update
programme.desc: Witness this historic flight, from the first manned launch from the US in nearly a decade to the first splashdown attempt since the Apollo era.

programme.title: Breakthrough - S01:E69 - Voyage to Venus
programme.desc: For the first time in decades, NASA is sending two new missions to Venus designed to study and explore the planet’s atmosphere and earth-like composition. Together, DAVINCI and VERITAS will provide a new, 360º view of Venus -- its history, and perhaps a window into Earth’s past as well.

programme.title: Breakthrough - S01:E75 - Artemis First Launch
programme.desc: This is an inside look at NASA's groundbreaking Artemis Program, the spacecraft, and the people who will bring humanity one step closer to the moon, Mars, and beyond.

programme.title: Breakthrough - S01:E94 - Artemis II Ready for the Moon
programme.desc: Explore the rockets, landers, vehicles, and space capsule paving the way for future Artemis missions to the lunar surface. And meet the engineers—and the machines—behind NASA's Commercial Lander Payload Services (CLPS) missions, which are revolutionizing humanity’s relationship with the Moon.

programme.title: The New Frontier - S02:E02 - Getting UpThere
programme.desc: Launching payloads into space is a very difficult task, historically rocket launches are the proverbial 'swords into ploughshares' Missiles designed to carry atomic warheads now send satellites and probes into the solar system. Ironically it's one of the few exploits Mankind undertakes that doesn't occur in nature.

programme.title: The New Frontier - S02:E03 - Orbit
programme.desc: The International Space Station is undoubtedly the jewel in the crown of low Earth orbit; observation post, research lab and class room. Equally however there are many other assets orbiting Earth that are even more important to our everyday lives; delivering communications, weather observation, global positioning and resource management the list is growing with every year.

programme.title: The New Frontier - S02:E04 - Shore to Shore
programme.desc: Our seafaring nature has translated well to the space age, seeking to sail out into the unknown in search of riches of one kind or another. While Europe and Asia continue their interest in the resource rich Moon, The United States and NASA have set their sights on nothing less than manned missions to Mars. Can they manage to go shore to shore on the most dangerous of unknown seas, deep space.

programme.title: The New Frontier - S02:E05 - Mars: Adapt or Leave
programme.desc: As the latest successes and failures come and go Mars continues to give up her secrets. Invisible clouds are revealed with ultraviolet light and the search for the source of methane continues with ExoMars. As we prepare to land humans on the red planet, getting there is one thing; staying long term is another, can we really conquor this planet?

programme.title: The New Frontier - S02:E06 - Emissaries
programme.desc: Our solar system is vast, from our own star the Sun to Earth is nearly 150 million kilometers or 1 Astronomical Unit. Jupiter is 5.2 AU distant and Pluto up to 48AU, the solar system extends far beyond this into interstellar space. We humans cannot yet travel that sort of distance, however w e can and do send our robots and probes in our place; and the results are astounding.

programme.title: Breakthrough - S01:E780 - Voyage Into The Sun Extended Version
programme.desc: For the first time in history, NASA’s Parker Solar Probe has pierced the Sun’s corona and is orbiting above its surface. Scientists have a front-row seat to better understand the sun and predict huge solar eruptions that can cause serious damage when they hit Earth.

programme.title: Breakthrough - S01:E63 - First Human Link
programme.desc: 65 million years ago, an immense space rock slammed into Earth, creating the equivalent of nuclear winter, killing all of the dinosaurs. Now, a team of scientists believes there was a witness to the catastrophe …a survivor that walked alongside T-rex … and that also allowed humans to be here today.

programme.title: The New Frontier - S02:E02 - Getting UpThere
programme.desc: Launching payloads into space is a very difficult task, historically rocket launches are the proverbial 'swords into ploughshares' Missiles designed to carry atomic warheads now send satellites and probes into the solar system. Ironically it's one of the few exploits Mankind undertakes that doesn't occur in nature.

programme.title: The New Frontier - S02:E03 - Orbit
programme.desc: The International Space Station is undoubtedly the jewel in the crown of low Earth orbit; observation post, research lab and class room. Equally however there are many other assets orbiting Earth that are even more important to our everyday lives; delivering communications, weather observation, global positioning and resource management the list is growing with every year.

programme.title: The New Frontier - S02:E04 - Shore to Shore
programme.desc: Our seafaring nature has translated well to the space age, seeking to sail out into the unknown in search of riches of one kind or another. While Europe and Asia continue their interest in the resource rich Moon, The United States and NASA have set their sights on nothing less than manned missions to Mars. Can they manage to go shore to shore on the most dangerous of unknown seas, deep space.

programme.title: The New Frontier - S02:E05 - Mars: Adapt or Leave
programme.desc: As the latest successes and failures come and go Mars continues to give up her secrets. Invisible clouds are revealed with ultraviolet light and the search for the source of methane continues with ExoMars. As we prepare to land humans on the red planet, getting there is one thing; staying long term is another, can we really conquor this planet?

programme.title: The New Frontier - S02:E06 - Emissaries
programme.desc: Our solar system is vast, from our own star the Sun to Earth is nearly 150 million kilometers or 1 Astronomical Unit. Jupiter is 5.2 AU distant and Pluto up to 48AU, the solar system extends far beyond this into interstellar space. We humans cannot yet travel that sort of distance, however w e can and do send our robots and probes in our place; and the results are astounding.

programme.title: Breakthrough - S01:E780 - Voyage Into The Sun Extended Version
programme.desc: For the first time in history, NASA’s Parker Solar Probe has pierced the Sun’s corona and is orbiting above its surface. Scientists have a front-row seat to better understand the sun and predict huge solar eruptions that can cause serious damage when they hit Earth.

programme.title: Breakthrough - S01:E63 - First Human Link
programme.desc: 65 million years ago, an immense space rock slammed into Earth, creating the equivalent of nuclear winter, killing all of the dinosaurs. Now, a team of scientists believes there was a witness to the catastrophe …a survivor that walked alongside T-rex … and that also allowed humans to be here today.
